lines.trans: Good morning, everyone! Welcome, Clara. Is everything ready?
Good morning! Yes, the counter is clean and the keys are ready.
The guest in room four is staying all week. Everything must be perfect!
Relax, Ernesto. The room is clean and the towels are dry.
I need to read the reservation book, yet I cannot find my glasses!
Are they in your coat pocket?
No, I only have my pen and three old receipts!
Look in the mirror behind the counter, boss.
Why would my glasses be in the... oh! They are on my head!
Right there on your forehead, safe and sound.
Not a word to anyone! Now smile when the bell rings.
Right now a taxi is pulling up at the gate.

meanings.note: Marks destination, clock time, and animate direct objects (personal a).

examples.trans: We are going to the station now.

examples.text: El desayuno empieza a las ocho.
examples.trans: Breakfast starts at eight o'clock.

meanings.note: Warm outer coat worn in cold or rainy weather.

examples.trans: The coat is here.

examples.text: Vemos los abrigos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the coats from the door.

meanings.note: Expresses sudden realization or understanding.

examples.trans: Ah, now I understand the map!
Oh really? What good news.

meanings.note: Ahora mismo means 'right now'.

examples.trans: I am heading there right now.
Now we have four free tables.

meanings.note: Points to something at medium distance or near the listener.

examples.text: Deja las llaves ahí en la mesa.
examples.trans: Leave the keys there on the table.
There comes the bus.

meanings.note: Agrees with the person welcomed (bienvenido, bienvenida, bienvenidos, bienvenidas).

examples.trans: It is a welcome piece.

examples.text: Déjemelo a mí. Vamos abajo a darle la bienvenida.
examples.trans: Leave it to me. Let us go down and welcome him.

meanings.note: Coat or trouser pocket.

examples.trans: The pocket is here.

examples.text: Vemos los bolsillos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the pockets from the door.

meanings.note: Often shortened colloquially in Spain to boli.

examples.trans: The ballpoint pen is here.

examples.text: Vemos los bolígrafos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the ballpoint pens from the door.

meanings.note: Shortens to buen before masculine singular nouns (buen viaje); ¡Buenos días! = Good morning!

examples.trans: Good morning, everyone!
The weather is very nice today.

meanings.note: Dolor de cabeza means 'headache'.

examples.trans: The head is here.

examples.text: Vemos las cabezas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the heads from the door.

meanings.note: Feminine counterpart of el cliente.

examples.trans: The guest is here.

examples.text: Vemos las clientas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the guests from the door.

meanings.note: Unaccented in statements and time clauses (interrogative: cuándo).

examples.trans: Let me know when the taxi arrives.

examples.text: Cuando llueve, huele a tierra mojada.
examples.trans: When it rains, it smells like wet earth.

meanings.note: Invariable cardinal number.

examples.trans: We have four tables inside.

examples.text: La habitación cuatro da al patio.
examples.trans: Room four looks out onto the courtyard.

meanings.note: Links possession, origin, material (de madera), and contents (taza de té).

examples.text: Es una mesa redonda de madera.
examples.trans: It is a round wooden table.

examples.text: Vengo de la estación de tren.
examples.trans: I am coming from the train station.

meanings.note: With a noun object (le debo la verdad), means 'to owe'; before an infinitive, means 'should / ought to'.

examples.text: Le debo diez euros de cambio.
examples.trans: I owe you ten euros in change.
Everything works as it should.

meanings.note: Mandatory contraction of preposition de + masculine article el.

examples.text: El bizcocho acaba de salir del horno.
examples.trans: The cake just came out of the oven.
I am a neighbour from the quarter.

meanings.note: Detrás de + noun means 'behind something'.

examples.text: El jardín está detrás de la casa.
examples.trans: The garden is behind the house.

examples.text: Hay otra página detrás del aviso.
examples.trans: There is another page behind the notice.

meanings.note: Masculine despite ending in -a: el día, ¡Buenos días!.

examples.trans: The day is here.

examples.text: Vemos los días desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the days from the door.

meanings.note: Definite article; also appears before feminine nouns starting with stressed /a/ (el agua, el asa).

examples.trans: The courtyard has plenty of light.
Pass me the reservation book.

meanings.note: Expresses location inside or on top of a surface (en la mesa = on the table).

examples.text: Las tazas están en la mesa.
examples.trans: The cups are on the table.

examples.text: Vivimos en Valencia todo el año.
examples.trans: We live in Valencia all year.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (o -> ue: encuentro).

examples.text: No encuentro mis gafas de leer.
examples.trans: I cannot find my reading glasses.
We found a terrific bakery.

meanings.note: Wall or bathroom mirror.

examples.trans: The mirror is here.

examples.text: Vemos los espejos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the mirrors from the door.

meanings.note: Pairs with locations (está en el patio) and temporary states (está caliente).

examples.trans: Breakfast is ready now.
Where are the brass keys?

frente.gloss: forehead; front (frente a = in front of)

meanings.en: forehead; front (frente a = in front of)
meanings.note: La frente (f) = forehead; frente a frente = face to face.

examples.trans: The forehead is here.

examples.text: Vemos las frentes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the foreheads from the door.

meanings.note: Plural-only feminine noun in Spain: las gafas.

examples.trans: Where did I leave my glasses?
He wears round glasses.

meanings.note: Plural habitaciones.

examples.trans: The room is here.

examples.text: Vemos las habitaciones desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the rooms from the door.

meanings.note: ¡Hasta luego! = See you later!; ¡Hasta mañana! = See you tomorrow!

examples.trans: Walk straight ahead as far as the bridge.
We are staying until Friday.

meanings.note: Ir a + infinitive expresses near future ('going to do').

examples.text: Voy a abrir la puerta ahora.
examples.trans: I am going to open the door now.
How is everything going this morning?

meanings.note: Feminine: la jefa.

examples.trans: The boss is here.

examples.text: Vemos los jefes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the bosss from the door.

meanings.note: Definite feminine singular article before nouns; direct-object feminine pronoun before/attached to verbs.

examples.text: La puerta del patio es azul.
examples.trans: The courtyard door is blue.
The room has plenty of light.

meanings.note: Used with feminine plural nouns and clock hours (las ocho).

examples.trans: The windows face the garden.
We have breakfast at eight.

meanings.note: Preterite 3rd sg/pl spells y: leyó, leyeron; past participle leído.

examples.text: Leo el periódico con el primer café.
examples.trans: I read the newspaper with my first coffee.

examples.text: Anoche leímos toda la carta juntos.
examples.trans: Last night we read the whole letter together.

meanings.note: Libro de reservas = reservation ledger.

examples.trans: The book is here.

examples.text: Vemos los libros desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the books from the door.

meanings.note: Opposite of sucio (dirty).

examples.trans: It is a clean piece.

examples.text: Aquí tiene un paño limpio y agua fría, Ernesto.
examples.trans: Here is a clean cloth and cold water, Ernesto.

meanings.note: With estar, means 'ready / all set'; with ser, means 'smart'.

examples.text: El té caliente ya está listo.
examples.trans: The hot tea is ready now.
She is a very smart architect.

meanings.note: Versatile everyday noun for door keys, shut-off valves, and spanners.

examples.trans: The key is here.

examples.text: Vemos las llaves desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the keys from the door.

meanings.note: Preterite 1st sg spells g -> gu: llegué.

examples.trans: I always arrive ten minutes early.

examples.text: El tren de Madrid llegó en punto.
examples.trans: The train from Madrid arrived on the dot.

meanings.note: ¡Hasta luego! is Spain's most common everyday farewell.

examples.text: Cruza el puente y luego gira.
examples.trans: Cross the bridge and then turn.
See you later, have a good day!

meanings.note: Plural mis (mi llave / mis llaves); unaccented, distinct from pronoun mí.

examples.trans: My suitcase is navy blue.

examples.text: Mis apuntes están en el bolsillo.
examples.trans: My notes are in my pocket.

mirar.gloss: to look; to look at; to watch

meanings.en: to look; to look at; to watch
meanings.note: Needs no preposition for 'at' (mira el reloj = look at the clock).

examples.text: Mira qué sol hace esta mañana.
examples.trans: Look how sunny it is this morning.

examples.text: Miramos el mapa antes de salir.
examples.trans: We look at the map before going out.

meanings.note: Agrees with the noun it describes.
In ahora mismo, meaning right now, mismo strengthens the time word ahora. Now comes from ahora; mismo supplies emphasis without agreeing with a person in this expression.

examples.trans: We have the same job.
I am busy right now.

meanings.note: Reception desk or shop counter.

examples.trans: The counter is here.

examples.text: Vemos los mostradores desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the counters from the door.

meanings.note: Requires no before the verb when nadie follows (no hay nadie).

examples.text: Todavía no hay nadie en el patio.
examples.trans: There is nobody in the courtyard yet.
Nobody knows this building better.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.trans: I need a pen to sign.
Do you all need another towel?

meanings.note: Ni... ni... = neither... nor...; ni una gota = not a single drop.

examples.text: No cae ni una sola gota.
examples.trans: Not a single drop is falling.

examples.text: No tengo ni papel ni bolígrafo.
examples.trans: I have neither paper nor pen.

meanings.note: Placed directly before the verb (or object pronouns) to negate a sentence.

examples.trans: Today it is not raining in Valencia.

examples.text: No se preocupe por la hora.
examples.trans: Do not worry about the time.

meanings.note: Ni una palabra = not a word.

examples.trans: The word is here.

examples.text: Vemos las palabras desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the words from the door.

meanings.note: Used alone as 'Perfect!'.

examples.trans: It is a perfect piece.

examples.text: La clienta de la habitación cuatro se queda toda la semana. ¡Todo debe estar perfecto!
examples.trans: The guest in room four is staying all week. Everything must be perfect!

meanings.note: Core contrast conjunction.

examples.text: Hace frío fuera, pero dentro se está bien.
examples.trans: It is cold outside, yet inside it is cosy.

examples.text: Es pequeño, pero tiene mucha luz.
examples.trans: It is small, but it has lots of light.

por.gloss: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)

meanings.en: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)
meanings.note: Por la mañana = in the morning; por favor = please; gracias por = thanks for.

examples.trans: We stroll through the old quarter.

examples.text: Por la mañana entra mucho sol.
examples.trans: In the morning plenty of sun comes in.

meanings.note: Covers room doors, street doors, and courtyard gates.

examples.trans: The door is here.

examples.text: Vemos las puertas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the doors from the door.

quedar.gloss: to remain / be left; to suit; to meet up (Spain); to stay (quedarse)

meanings.en: to remain / be left; to suit; to meet up (Spain); to stay (quedarse)
meanings.note: Versatile verb: quedan dos ('two left'), le queda bien ('suits you'), quedar al mediodía ('meet at noon'), quedarse ('stay').

examples.trans: Only two vacant rooms are left.

examples.text: Esa chaqueta te queda muy bien.
examples.trans: That jacket suits you very well.

qué.gloss: what?; which?; how / what a! (in exclamations)

meanings.en: what?; which?; how / what a! (in exclamations)
meanings.note: Used in questions (¿qué hora es?) and exclamations (¡qué alivio!).

examples.trans: What time is it right now?
What a bright morning!

meanings.note: Paper receipt.

examples.trans: The receipt is here.

examples.text: Vemos los recibos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the receipts from the door.

meanings.note: Tener una reserva = to have a booking.

examples.trans: The reservation is here.

examples.text: Vemos las reservas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the reservations from the door.

meanings.note: Estar a salvo = to be safe; sano y salvo = safe and sound.

examples.trans: It is a safe piece.

examples.text: Ahí mismo, en la frente, sanas y salvas.
examples.trans: Right there on your forehead, safe and sound.

sano.gloss: healthy; sound (sano y salvo = safe and sound)

meanings.en: healthy; sound (sano y salvo = safe and sound)
meanings.note: Sanas y salvas agrees with feminine plural nouns like tazas.

examples.trans: It is a healthy piece.

examples.text: Ahí mismo, en la frente, sanas y salvas.
examples.trans: Right there on your forehead, safe and sound.

se.gloss: himself / herself / yourself / themselves; impersonal one

meanings.en: himself / herself / yourself / themselves; impersonal one
meanings.note: Reflexive, reciprocal, passive/impersonal pronoun, and indirect object le/les before lo/la.

examples.trans: The door opens slowly.

examples.text: Aquí se oye el canto de los pájaros.
examples.trans: Here you can hear the birds singing.

meanings.note: Toallas secas = dry towels.

examples.trans: It is a dry piece.

examples.text: ¡Javier lo dejó ahí cuando cogió la toalla seca!
examples.trans: Javier set it down there when he took the dry towel!

meanings.note: Fin de semana = weekend; la semana que viene = next week.

examples.trans: The week is here.

examples.text: Vemos las semanas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the weeks from the door.

solo.gloss: only; just (also adj solo/sola = alone / single)

meanings.en: only; just (also adj solo/sola = alone / single)
meanings.note: Unaccented in modern RAE spelling; café solo = black espresso.

examples.trans: I only need five more minutes.
Only a single room remains vacant.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (o -> ue: suena).

examples.text: El despertador suena a las seis y media.
examples.trans: The alarm clock rings at six thirty.

examples.text: El piano sonaba cálido bajo la lluvia.
examples.trans: The piano sounded warm in the rain.

meanings.note: Conjugates like reír (sonrío, sonrió); imperative plural: ¡sonreíd!.

examples.text: La panadera siempre sonríe al abrir el horno.
examples.trans: The baker always smiles when opening the oven.

examples.text: Al probar el bizcocho, sonrió enseguida.
examples.trans: Upon tasting the cake, he smiled right away.

meanings.note: Accented sí means 'yes' (distinct from unaccented si = 'if').

examples.trans: Yes, the room is ready.
Of course, come right in!

meanings.note: Plural los taxis.

examples.trans: The taxi is here.

examples.text: Vemos los taxis desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the taxis from the door.

tener.gloss: to have; to have to (tener que + inf)

meanings.en: to have; to have to (tener que + inf)
meanings.note: Used in idioms: tener hambre/frío/miedo/prisa/razón; tener que = must.

examples.trans: We have eight quiet rooms.

examples.text: Tengo que cerrar la ventana ahora.
examples.trans: I have to close the window now.

meanings.note: Tocar el timbre = ring the bell.

examples.trans: The bell is here.

examples.text: Vemos los timbres desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the bells from the door.

meanings.note: Clean bath or hand towel.

examples.trans: The towel is here.

examples.text: Vemos las toallas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the towels from the door.

meanings.note: Todo el día = the whole day; todo el mundo = everyone; sobre todo = mostly.

examples.text: Todo está limpio y en su sitio.
examples.trans: Everything is clean and in its place.

examples.text: Camina todo recto por esta calle.
examples.trans: Walk straight ahead down this street.

meanings.note: Said alone to reassure someone ('Easy, don't worry!').

examples.trans: It is a quiet piece.

examples.text: Seca, calentita y tranquila. Ahora decidme qué falta.
examples.trans: Dry, warm, and quiet. Now tell me what is missing.

meanings.note: Invariable cardinal number.

examples.text: Ponemos tres mesas bajo el árbol.
examples.trans: We set three tables under the tree.
Start with three short sentences.

meanings.note: Forms: un (m sg), una (f sg), unos (m pl 'some/about'), unas (f pl).

examples.text: Quiero un café caliente, por favor.
examples.trans: I would like a hot coffee, please.

examples.text: Hay una mesa libre en el patio.
examples.trans: There is a free table in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Before a noun (un viejo amigo), means 'long-standing / dear old'.

examples.trans: It is an old piece.
The old sunny attic room... follow me, quickly!

meanings.note: Changes to e before words starting with /i/ sound (i- or hi-).

examples.text: Servimos café caliente y pan fresco.
examples.trans: We serve hot coffee and fresh bread.
It is quarter past seven.
